a)Current Profile -Diwakar Patwari  is the Mukhiya of Matiyariya Panchayat.
b)Socio-Political Brief - He contested his first-ever election in 2021 and became the Mukhiya with more than 1000 votes. He was sent to jail for three months right after he filed his nomination. The case was filed by Zamindars regarding a land dispute. He won his election while he was in jail. Before 2021, more than 50 bighas of his land has been illegally occupied by zamindars. He has been fighting to get his land back from them. In 2019 he built a small playground on his own land for the children of his panchayat. He rehabilitated more than 80 households who lost their homes in the 2017 floods in a place called Sherpur. His grandfather was a JP Senani. There are more than 80 households in his family in the panchayat.
c)Financial Activities - Financially he is strong. He owns 20 bigha of agricultural land, which is also his only source of income.
d)Area|Community Influence - He has good influence over the people of his panchayat and he is the popular face of the Gaunaha block in the Tharu community. About 45% population of the population of the his panchayat is Tharu and they support him. About 20% muslim in his panchayat also support him because he has rehabilitated many of them.
e)Criminal Cases - Yes, Civil dispute relating to land.
f)Public perception -He is seen as a robin hood of his panchayat. He has always worked for the poor and underprivileged people of his panchayat.
g)Recent Activities - He built a small children’s playground on his own land.

Profile:
a)Current Profile -Diwakar Patwari is the Mukhiya of Matiyariya Panchayat.
b)Socio-Political Brief - He contested his first-ever election in 2021 and became the Mukhiya with more than 1000 votes. He was sent to jail for three months right after he filed his nomination. The case was filed by Zamindars regarding a land dispute. He won his election while he was in jail. Before 2021, more than 50 bighas of his land has been illegally occupied by zamindars. He has been fighting to get his land back from them. In 2019 he built a small playground on his own land for the children of his panchayat. He rehabilitated more than 80 households who lost their homes in the 2017 floods in a place called Sherpur. His grandfather was a JP Senani. There are more than 80 households in his family in the panchayat.
c)Financial Activities - Financially he is strong. He owns 20 bigha of agricultural land, which is also his only source of income.
d)Area|Community Influence - He has good influence over the people of his panchayat and he is the popular face of the Gaunaha block in the Tharu community. About 45% population of the population of the his panchayat is Tharu and they support him. About 20% muslim in his panchayat also support him because he has rehabilitated many of them.
e)Criminal Cases - Yes, Civil dispute relating to land.
f)Public perception -He is seen as a robin hood of his panchayat. He has always worked for the poor and underprivileged people of his panchayat.
g)Recent Activities - He built a small children’s playground on his own land.

Name: Nitish Kharwar

Current Position - Nitish Kharwar is the Zila Sachiv of Yuva Kharwar Mahasabha Bihar (a non-registered organization).
Socio-Political Brief - He received his B.A. from Baba Bhagwat Rai College in Bettiah. In 2018,  Nitish Kharwar, along with Naveen Kharwar of Gaunaha Block founded "Yuva Kharwar Mahasabha Bihar" to assist students in obtaining caste certificates in order to apply for various government jobs. This organization acts as a pressure group for government officials who have refused to grant caste certificates to Kharwar community members.
This organization also conducts door-to-door campaigns for the Kharwar community, organizes small sabhas, and educates people about the value of education in lifting poor households out of poverty.
Financial Activities - He is from a lower middle-class household and owns approximately 5 acres of farmland.
Area | Community influence - He has a strong influence over the ST community, particularly Kharwars, and approximately 3000-3500 people live in Nautan Block.
No criminal case (if any) - No
Public Perception - He is young, educated, and knows how to elevate the voice of society's oppressed class. Nitish is doing an outstanding job of assisting Kharwar community students in obtaining government jobs.  This is based on his personal experience of not receiving a government job despite passing the SSC exam and not having the updated caste certificate. He is socially active and wants to make a difference in the lives of marginalized communities.
